note: The everyday Talk-to conversation, opened when the follower has asked nothing. Kept apart from dialogs.json because it does not change with play - it is what the follower is, not what it is currently up to; the trees in dialogs.json are the ones the follower OPENS, which is a different job. Bundled only, never copied out or edited in game. Three rules hold this together. Every choice leads to a node where the PLAYER says that exact line: the game works that way and players read it that way - the option is the sentence you are about to speak, not a summary of it. Jumping straight to a menu instead reads as the click having gone astray, and an option whose node says something slightly different reads as a bug, because it is one. A test enforces the match. Nothing here is a feature list: what the follower can do comes out as habits and grievances, the way a person describes their job, because a companion reciting its own capabilities is a manual with a face. And a branch never replays a line already read - hence the -menu nodes, which re-offer the follow-ups without the preamble. A node with "when" is built only while every fact it names holds, and a fact with ! only while it does not: lowish (the mood band is low or down), the band itself (low, down, even, good, high), and errands and thrall-outfits (the build has them). Of the nodes sharing an id exactly one is built, in its place in the list. moods: what the day summary says of each mood band; any other band gets the ordinary one.

Worth saying out loud - the follower turning up to a mage fight in melee gear is the one thing about this that looks broken rather than deliberate.

nodes.note: The one page in the script that is different every time it is read. Everything in it is already counted - the tallies exist for the milestone lines - so this is the same memory said as a sentence rather than as a number, which is what makes it sound like somebody who was there rather than a scoreboard. how-today-a's pages are that summary, built on each visit.

says: It's the job. Every rat, every level, every time you've gone down in front of me.
It isn't judgement. Somebody should, that's all.
I remember it between days, too. You come back and the number's still there.

When it's gone well I stand one way. When it hasn't, I stand another.

If I ever ask you to take me somewhere, come and talk to me and I'll say where.
I won't ask twice. It's not that sort of arrangement.
